ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a sinusoidal AC power source labeled 20/√2 V, followed by a bridge rectifier circuit and a filter capacitor. The output after rectification and filtering passes through the series resistor Rs, and on the right side there is a Zener diode labeled 5 V, 1/4 W connected in parallel with the load resistor RL. Reasoning: According to the method given in the problem, regard the maximum DC voltage after bridge rectification plus capacitance as the AC peak value. Given Vrms = 20/√2 V, therefore the peak value Vpeak = √2 × 20/√2 = 20 V. The rated power of the Zener diode is 1/4 W, and the voltage regulation value is 5 V, so the maximum safe Zener current Iz,max = Pz/Vz = 0.25/5 = 0.05 A. Considering all possible RL, the most dangerous case is RL → ∞, at which time the load takes no current, and all the current flowing through Rs enters the Zener diode. To avoid burning it out, (20 - 5)/Rs ≤ 0.05 is needed, therefore Rs ≥ 15/0.05 = 300 Ω. So the minimum value of Rs is 300 Ω.

method.method_draft: From the figure, treat the bridge rectifier plus capacitor as producing a maximum DC level equal to the sinusoidal peak. The text gives Vrms = 20/sqrt(2) V, so Vpeak = sqrt(2)*Vrms = 20 V. The shunt Zener is rated 5 V and 1/4 W, so its maximum safe current is Iz,max = 0.25/5 = 0.05 A. Considering all RL, the worst case for Zener burnout is RL -> infinity, because no load current is drawn and all current through Rs goes into the Zener. Therefore require (20 - 5)/Rs <= 0.05, giving Rs >= 300 ohm; the minimum Rs is 300 ohm.

method.method_draft: First identify the rectified capacitor voltage from the shown bridge-and-capacitor stage. With the text value Vrms = 20/sqrt(2) V, the sinusoidal peak, and hence the maximum capacitor voltage, is 20 V. During regulation the output node is clamped to Vz = 5 V. By KCL at the output node, the series-resistor current is (20 - 5)/Rs and it splits as Iz + IL, where IL = 5/RL. Thus Iz(RL) = 15/Rs - 5/RL. Over all possible positive RL values, Iz is largest when 5/RL is smallest, i.e. RL -> infinity. Enforce the Zener rating Pz = Vz Iz <= 1/4 W, so Iz <= 0.05 A. Hence 15/Rs <= 0.05, giving Rs >= 300 ohm.
